item.title: Search continues for 6 missing at sea as MSAF urges mariners to heed weather warnings
item.description: As the search continues for the 6 people who were travelling in a fibre glass boat between Namuka and Fulaga in the Lau Group, m ariners in maritme areas across Fiji are being urged to strictly follow active weather warnings. According to reports received by MSAF, the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre (JRCC) Fiji was notified yesterday that a half-cabin fibre glass boat powered by a 40-horsepower o
item.content:encoded:
As the search continues for the 6 people who were travelling in a fibre glass boat between Namuka and Fulaga in the Lau Group, m ariners in maritme areas across Fiji are being urged to strictly follow active weather warnings.

According to reports received by MSAF, the Joint Rescue Coordination Centre (JRCC) Fiji was notified yesterday that a half-cabin fibre glass boat powered by a 40-horsepower outboard engine had failed to arrive at its destination.

The vessel reportedly departed Namuka Island at around 10am yesterday bound for Fulaga Island.

Three fibre glass boats left Namuka that morning while two arrived safely in Fulaga, the third remains overdue with six people on board.

Following the report, JRCC Fiji, operating from the Vuvale Maritime Essential Services Centre (MESC), immediately activated search and rescue operations.

Navy Search and Rescue (SAR) mission coordinators have been working through the night, coordinating with government agencies, nearby vessels, and community contacts across the area.

Plans are underway to deploy both sea and air search assets today to widen the search effort.

Authorities are concerned that the missing vessel may not have been carrying essential life-saving equipment.

They say search operations are also being made more difficult by deteriorating weather conditions, including strong winds and rough to very rough seas.

They say despite these challenges, every effort remains focused on locating the vessel and bringing its occupants to safety.

M SAF is asking all mariners travelling between Namuka, Fulaga, and surrounding waters to keep a vigilant lookout for a white half-cabin fibreglass boat powered by a 40-horsepowe r outboard engine and its six occupants.

Anyone who sights the vessel or has information that could assist the search is urged to contact JRCC Fiji immediately on the toll-free number 1539 or report it to the nearest Police Station .

MSAF also reminds all mariners to take the nationwide Strong Wind Warning, issued on Thursday, 6 August 2026, seriously. The warning advises of southeasterly winds of 20 to 30 knots and rough to very rough sea conditions across affected areas.

In light of this incident, MSAF is reminding vessel owners and small-boat operators of their responsibilities to ensure safe operations at sea.

The search remains active, and further updates will be provided through official channels as confirmed information becomes available.

item.title: Record $3.51 billion revenue collected for 2025-2026 financial year
item.description: The Fiji Revenue and Customs Service has collected net revenue of $3.510 billion for the financial year ended 31st July 2026—the highest annual revenue collection recorded by the Service. FRCS says the result is $136.2 million, or 4 percent, above the Government’s annual forecast of $3.374 billion.
item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Revenue and Customs Service has collected net revenue of $3.510 billion for the financial year ended 31st July 2026—the highest annual revenue collection recorded by the Service.

FRCS says the result is $136.2 million, or 4 percent, above the Government’s annual forecast of $3.374 billion.

They say it is also $25.8 million, or 0.7 percent, higher than the $3.485 billion collected in the previous financial year.

FRCS Chief Executive Officer Udit Singh says the result demonstrated the resilience of Fiji’s economy despite geopolitical uncertainty, international fuel-supply pressures, imported inflation and softer expectations for tourism and consumer activity.

He says this record result reflects the strength of Fiji’s underlying business and employment base.

Singh says businesses continued to operate and contribute, employers maintained jobs and wages, trade remained active, and taxpayers continued to support the country despite a challenging economic environment.

FRCS says growth was led by Net Income Tax, which increased by $53.7 million, Net Customs collections, which increased by $46.6 million, and Departure Tax, which increased by $43.7 million.

Within these categories, PAYE increased by $37.9 million and Company Income Tax rose by $28.3 million.

FRCS says these results point to continued resilience in formal employment, wages, and business profitability.

They say Fiscal Duty, Domestic Excise Duty, Withholding Tax, and Import Excise Duty also recorded positive annual growth.

FRCS confirms Net VAT declined by $102.8 million compared with the previous year, principally reflecting the reduction in the VAT rate from 15 percent to 12.5 percent, together with refund and payment-timing effects.

They say the decline should therefore not be interpreted as an equivalent reduction in underlying economic activity.

FRCS says the July collection was $288.8 million, which was $16.6 million below forecast and $22.3 million below July 2025.

They say the softer monthly result was influenced by the timing of Company Income Tax payments and higher refunds.

The Service says nevertheless, the strong performance over the preceding eleven months enabled FRCS to finish the year well above its annual forecast.

Singh says the result was broadly consistent with the Reserve Bank of Fiji’s assessment that the economy continues to grow, although at a slower pace and with elevated risks from fuel prices, inflation, and global uncertainty.

He says we should view this achievement with confidence but not complacency.

Singh stresses the economic risks remain real, but the breadth of the revenue result shows that Fiji enters the new financial year with a resilient economic and fiscal foundation.

The CEO thanked Fiji’s taxpayers, businesses, employers, importers, exporters, customs brokers, and tax agents for their contribution.

He says this achievement belongs first and foremost to Fiji’s taxpayers.

Singh stresses every dollar collected supports essential public services, including healthcare, education, infrastructure, social assistance, and border protection.

He also thanked the FRCS Board for its leadership and governance, their staff for their professionalism and commitment, and the Government, Ministry of Finance, Reserve Bank of Fiji and their partner agencies for their continued cooperation and support.

item.title: Union claims EFL executives received higher pay as workers await wage increases
item.description: Concerns have been raised after workers at Energy Fiji Limited represented by the Construction Energy and Timber Workers Union of Fiji claims they have gone three years without a wage increase while senior executives have received higher remuneration. In a statement, the union claims recent figures show the total remuneration for EFL's Chief Executive Officer and Executive Management Group increas
item.content:encoded:
Concerns have been raised after workers at Energy Fiji Limited represented by the Construction Energy and Timber Workers Union of Fiji claims they have gone three years without a wage increase while senior executives have received higher remuneration.

In a statement, the union claims recent figures show the total remuneration for EFL's Chief Executive Officer and Executive Management Group increased from $3.309 million in 2024 to $3.756 million in 2025 .

The union says its members are still waiting for wage increases for 2024, 2025 and 2026, alleging that EFL has not settled the union's log of claims for those years.

They say the difference in pay raises raises concerns about fairness and equitable treatment of workers, arguing that employees who contribute to EFL's operations should also be fairly compensated.

The union says rewarding senior management while delaying wage settlements for union members affects staff morale and undermines trust.

They are calling on EFL to enter into what it describes as genuine, good-faith negotiations to resolve the outstanding wage claims and reach a fair outcome for its members.

The union says it remains committed to constructive industrial relations but believes wage increases should be distributed fairly and consistently across the organisation rather than benefiting only senior management.

They are also urging EFL's Board and executive leadership to begin negotiations without delay and settle the outstanding claims.

We have sent questions to Energy Fiji Limited.

item.title: Parents urged to know their children's whereabouts following Wailoku tragedy
item.description: Parents and guardians are being urged to know where their children are at all times following the tragic death of the 12-year-old boy whose body was found in Wailoku after he was reported missing. The Ministry of Women, Children and Social Protection says the heartbreaking incident is a reminder that protecting children is a shared responsibility that begins at home and extends throughout communit
item.content:encoded:
Parents and guardians are being urged to know where their children are at all times following the tragic death of the 12-year-old boy whose body was found in Wailoku after he was reported missing.

The Ministry of Women, Children and Social Protection says the heartbreaking incident is a reminder that protecting children is a shared responsibility that begins at home and extends throughout communities.

It has extended its condolences to the boy's parents, family, loved ones, classmates and the wider community.

While Police continue their investigation into the case, the Ministry says it will not speculate on the circumstances surrounding the boy's death and is urging anyone with information that could assist Police to come forward.

The Ministry says parents and guardians have a fundamental responsibility to know where their children are, who they are with and when they are expected to return home.

It is also calling on parents to take an active interest in their children's daily activities, friendships, online interactions and emotional wellbeing, saying open communication and regular engagement can help identify concerns early and reduce risks.

The Ministry stresses that child protection cannot be left to families alone, saying neighbours, relatives, teachers, faith leaders, youth leaders and community members all have a role to play in safeguarding children and should not ignore warning signs if a child's safety may be at risk.

It is also urging adults who host children for sleepovers or extended visits to ensure parents or guardians know the child's whereabouts and have given permission, saying a simple phone call can make the difference between a child being safe and a family experiencing unimaginable distress.

The Ministry has also raised concerns about children being left in the care of grandparents or extended family members following parental separation, remarriage or migration, stressing that while relatives often provide valuable care, biological parents remain responsible for their children's safety, development and wellbeing.

It says Government programmes and laws alone cannot keep children safe, and protecting children requires vigilance, responsibility and action from every parent, caregiver and community.

The Ministry is encouraging members of the public to seek help through the Child Helpline on 1325 , the National Domestic Violence Helpline on 1560 , the Social Protection Helpline on 1561 , or to contact Police on 917 or the nearest police station to report a missing child, suspected abuse or information relating to an investigation.

The Ministry says protecting children begins at home and is urging parents and guardians to remain vigilant and always know the whereabouts of their children.

item.title: Nouzab Fareed to be sentenced on 27th August
item.description: Former Fijian Holdings Limited Chief Executive Officer Nouzab Fareed will be sentenced on 27th August for indecently assaulting a woman in his office as his lawyers seek a suspended sentence. Fareed 's lawyer Hemendra Nagin says they are also seeking a non-conviction for his client.
item.content:encoded:
Former Fijian Holdings Limited Chief Executive Officer Nouzab Fareed will be sentenced on 27th August for indecently assaulting a woman in his office as his lawyers seek a suspended sentence.

Fareed 's lawyer Hemendra Nagin says they are also seeking a non-conviction for his client.

Fareed appeared before Magistrate Josaia Waqaivolavola this morning.

State Prosecutor Sadaf Shameem told the Court that they are seeking a conviction and a custodial sentence.

The tariff for this is 12 months to 4 years.

item.title: One charged, three in custody after cocaine, meth and marijuana seizures
item.description: A joint task force raid on Nadi Back Road has resulted in the arrest of one man and the seizure of cocaine, methamphetamine and marijuana, while three more men remain in Police custody following two separate drug raids in Nadi and Natabua. Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations, Kasiano Vusonilawe says the raid on Nadi Back Road was carried out on Wednesday by the Joint Task Force comprising
item.content:encoded:
A joint task force raid on Nadi Back Road has resulted in the arrest of one man and the seizure of cocaine, methamphetamine and marijuana, while three more men remain in Police custody following two separate drug raids in Nadi and Natabua.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Operations, Kasiano Vusonilawe says the raid on Nadi Back Road was carried out on Wednesday by the Joint Task Force comprising the Fiji Police Force, the Republic of Fiji Military Forces and the Fiji Detector Dog Unit.

Vusonilawe says white substances seized during the operation tested positive for cocaine and methamphetamine, while dried leaves were confirmed to be marijuana.

He says the suspect has been charged with one count of unlawful possession of illicit drugs and will appear in the Nadi Magistrates' Court today.

The Assistant Commissioner says two more Joint Task Force raids were carried out yesterday at a car wash in Nadi and a home in Natabua.

He says the operations resulted in the seizure of white substances believed to be illicit drugs, and three men were arrested.

Vusonilawe says the three men remain in Police custody while the seized substances have been sent for analysis.

Meanwhile, the suspect arrested during another Joint Task Force raid in Lautoka on Tuesday, following the seizure of methamphetamine, has been charged and appeared in the Lautoka Magistrates' Court yesterday.

Police are urging people to report drug-related activities by calling the Crime Stoppers line on 1681.
